title: Which design sits at a far position of the border?
description: The design at positions ninety nine, one hundred and twenty two and one hundred and forty eight of the saree border is found by dividing each position by three and reading the remainder.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing a position by three gives a remainder, and the remainder tells which design sits there. Watch for students who ignore the remainder and name the design of the nearest multiple of three.

source: Find the design at positions 99, 122 and 148 by dividing eac
video_script.why: A learner sees that dividing a position by three gives a remainder that decides the design.
video_script.substitution: the book's saree border that repeats the designs A, B and C, with the positions ninety nine, one hundred and twenty two and one hundred and forty eight
video_script.anchor: the saree border of the book, with far positions divided by three
video_script.wrong_answer: position one hundred and twenty two is design C
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says position one hundred and twenty two is design C because it is close to a multiple of three. The remainder is two, which is design B, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Position ninety nine holds design C, and position one hundred and twenty two holds design B. Position one hundred and forty eight holds design eigh.

final_answer.value: Position 99 is C, position 122 is B, position 148 is A
final_answer.spoken: position ninety nine is C, position one hundred and twenty two is B, position one hundred and forty eight is eigh

maths_rules: the border repeats A, B, C with A at 1, B at 2, C at 3, so C is at every multiple of 3
99 / 3 = 33, remainder 0, a multiple of 3, so design C
122 / 3 = 40, remainder 2; 3 x 41 = 123 and 122 is one less, so design B
148 / 3 = 49, remainder 1; 3 x 50 = 150 and 148 is two less, so design A
check: position 1 has remainder 1 and is A, position 2 has remainder 2 and is B, position 3 has remainder 0 and is C
Keeko test: 123 = 3 x 41 holds C, so 122 is one place before and holds B, not C
video_script.design: The border stays on the board; each far position is divided by three, the remainder is read, and the design is placed by counting back from the nearest multiple of three.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is another question about the saree border in your book. The designs eigh, B and C repeat in order.
<bookmark mark='pos'/>The positions are ninety nine, one hundred and twenty two, and one hundred and forty eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Counting that far would take long. Which design sits at each position?

beats.on_screen: the border and the three positions stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: divide a position by 3; what is left over is the remainder; design C is at every multiple of 3, B is one place before, A is two places before

marks.divide: a position is split into full sets of three
marks.rem: the leftover places are circled and labelled remainder
marks.mult: design C is lit at every multiple of three, with B and A just before it

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Dividing a position by three shows how many full sets of three it holds.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>What is left over is called the remainder.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Design C sits at every multiple of three. Design B is one place before it, and design eigh is two places before.

beats.on_screen: Given: the border repeats A, B, C; positions 99, 122 and 148
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the positions ninety nine, one hundred and twenty two, and one hundred and forty eight.

beats.on_screen: To find: the design at each position, by dividing by 3

marks.find: the words design and divide by 3 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the design at each position, by dividing by three.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 99 ÷ 3 = 33, remainder 0; 99 is a multiple of 3, so design C

marks.design: design C is lit at position 99

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step one, divide ninety nine by three. Thirty three threes fit exactly.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>The remainder is zero, so ninety nine is a multiple of three.
<bookmark mark='design'/>That position holds design C.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 122 ÷ 3 = 40, remainder 2; 3 × 41 = 123 and 122 is one less, so design B

marks.near: 3 × 41 = 123 is written, and 122 is marked one place before it
marks.design: design B is lit at position 122

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step two, divide one hundred and twenty two by three. Forty threes fit, and the remainder is two.
<bookmark mark='near'/>Three times forty one is one hundred and twenty three. One hundred and twenty two is one less.
<bookmark mark='design'/>That position holds design B.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 148 ÷ 3 = 49, remainder 1; 3 × 50 = 150 and 148 is two less, so design A

marks.near: 3 × 50 = 150 is written, and 148 is marked two places before it
marks.design: design A is lit at position 148

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide one hundred and forty eight by three. Forty nine threes fit, and the remainder is one.
<bookmark mark='near'/>Three times fifty is one hundred and fifty, and one hundred and forty eight is two less.
<bookmark mark='design'/>That position holds design eigh.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check on the first three positions: 1 has remainder 1 and is A; 2 has remainder 2 and is B; 3 has remainder 0 and is C

marks.one: position 1 is marked remainder 1, design A
marks.two: position 2 is marked remainder 2, design B
marks.three: position 3 is marked remainder 0, design C

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, check the remainders on the first three positions. Position one has remainder one, and holds design eigh.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Position two has remainder two, and holds design B.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Position three has remainder zero, and holds design C.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Position 99 is C, position 122 is B, position 148 is A
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Position ninety nine holds design C, and position one hundred and twenty two holds design B. Position one hundred and forty eight holds design eigh.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks position one hundred and twenty two is design C. It is close to a multiple of three.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Position one hundred and twenty three is three times forty one, so that position is design C.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Position one hundred and twenty two is one place before it.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A remainder of two means design B, not design C.
